1) the use of regulated deficit irrigation (RDI) can be used to achieve high quality grape production with less water consumption; 2) the use of RDI is based on the maintenance of a moderate water stress in the grapevine, and 3) this water stress can be achieved by the use of a suitable physiological indicator, such as midday stem water potentials, and by setting suitable thresholds.

the development of an irrigation scheduling method for precision irrigation in grapevires based on midday stem water potentials.
the application of a physiological index (midday [psi]S) to achieve a RDI in grapevines.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the midday [PsiS] is a suitable irrigation scheduling index to achieve RDI and precision irrigation on grapevines.
regulated deficit irrigation is a useful strategy to achieve high quality wines, with a significant reduction in water application, without yield losses.

a midday stem water pressure potential of -1.0 MPa (T2), imposed from post-setting to veraison is recommended for RDI application to achieve high quality berries in grapevines.

the midday stem water potentials thresholds proposed in this paper can be used to manage regulated deficit irrigation and irrigation scheduling on vineyards.
